relevance_note: The paper reports one child with a germline TNFAIP3 variant ("a heterozygous missense variant in the TNFAIP3 gene (c.1733C>T; p.Ser578Phe) was identified"), with individual-level detail in Table 1 and in the text, and describes the carrier mother and the tested father.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown file (main text, Table 1, Table 2, references). In scope: the one child carrying a TNFAIP3 variant (Table 1 row 3, labelled 'Table 1 #3'), the mother (same variant, clinically asymptomatic) and the father (tested, variant absent). The other five cohort children (rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 6) have no TNFAIP3 variant and no HA20 diagnosis, so they get no rows; their number is in publications.cohort_size_as_stated (6). The paper never labels the TNFAIP3 child individually, so the label follows rule (v4) 'Table <n> #<value>' using the 'Patient' column value 3; the mother and father follow rule 2 ('mother of Table 1 #3', 'father of Table 1 #3'). The child's sex and age at first cytopenia come from the Table 1 row ('| 3 | F | 3 |'). Variant fields: the variant is described in the Results text for that child and in the table cell 'TNFAIP3 VUS'; the 'VUS' wording is tied to the detected variant ('the detected variant ... is currently classified as a VUS'), so it is recorded as the authors' classification for this child. The cohort-level sentence 'Genetic variants were classified according to ... criteria as pathogenic, likely pathogenic, or VUS' (Methods) was not used. No stacking of ' / ' values was needed: no cell used by an in-scope person contains stacked values, so D-31 changes nothing here. Contradiction found: the text says 'no molecularly confirmed inborn error of immunity was established in this cohort', while it also states that variants in TNFAIP3 are associated with A20 haploinsufficiency; the child's disease label was therefore left as the paper's own 'Evans syndrome'. Age at first cytopenia (3 years) is recorded as age at onset of the haematological disease, not as an age at diagnosis; no separate age at diagnosis is printed. Table 2 gives no per-patient data for the TNFAIP3 child and was used only for the cohort-level numbers. Table 1's 'No' cells in the AIN, IM > 1 and Second-Line columns are the paper's own per-patient negative answers (column headings 'AIN', 'IM > 1', 'Second-Line'), so they were recorded as excluded for the child; the Table 2 cell 'Defined PID/Secondary Evans | 0 (0%)' is a count without names and excludes nobody, and the Table 1 'Genetic Finding' cell for this child ('TNFAIP3 VUS') is not a clinical feature, so no phenotypic_features row was made for either. The child's treatment was taken from the cohort sentence on first-line therapy plus the child's own 'Second-Line: No' cell. The mother's sentence ('the mother was clinically asymptomatic, with no history of autoimmune or autoinflammatory disease') is a general statement about her whole health, so it is recorded as one phenotypic_features row in the paper's own words and excludes no individual checklist item; is_proband is left null because the paper never calls anyone a proband or index case and never identifies a single case-report patient. clinical_diagnosis_basis is left 'not reported' for every person because the paper states only cohort-level diagnostic definitions and never says per person how the diagnosis was made. Table 1 was transcribed by hand, not by script; I checked each cell I used against the Markdown table.

study_type.span: This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at the Pediatric Hematology Unit of the University Hospital of Ioannina, a tertiary referral center in Epirus, Northwestern Greece.

n_patients_reported.span: Whole-exome sequencing performed in three patients identified a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant of uncertain significance in one case; no pathogenic variants were detected.

cohort_size_as_stated.span: Six children (4 males) were included, with a median age at first cytopenia of 7 years (range 3–15) and a median follow-up of 8 years (range 1–13).
